newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: Roche, Bayer, set U.S. over-the-counter venture.
newsitem.headline: Roche, Bayer, set U.S. over-the-counter venture.

text.p: Roche Holding AG and the U.S. subsidiary of German pharmaceuticals firm Bayer AG have signed a letter of intent to form a 50-50 joint venture to market several over-the-counter drugs in the United States, Roche said Monday.
Subject to approval by authorities, the joint venture will combine the companies' U.S. over-the-counter businesses in analgesics and women's health products.
Bayer aspirin will be excluded from the deal.
The deal will also exclude Bayer brands Alka-Seltzer, Alka-Seltzer Plus, One-A-Day and Flintstones vitamins.
Financial terms of the venture were not disclosed.

Brands included in the joint venture will be Roche's Aleve analgesic and Femstat 3 vaginal yeast infection treatment, as well as Bayer's Actron and Vanquish analgesics, Midol menstrual pain reliever and Mycelex-7 vaginal yeast infection treatment.
Bayer will be responsible for sales and marketing of the joint venture within its overall consumer care portfolio.

The agreement follows acquisition in June 1996 by Roche of a 50 percent stake held by Proctor & Gamble in another 50-50 joint venture. That agreement called for P&G to market Roche's Aleve and Femstat 3 brands in the U.S. market.
The new venture calls for these marketing and distribution services to be transferred to Bayer from P&G, which will maintain responsibility for professional, or doctors' sales, until the end of 1997.
Roche and Bayer said the move would enhance the position of both firms in the U.S. over-the-counter health care market.

Beat Alpiger, an analyst at Bank Julius Baer, said the move would provide the companies with a strong basis in the U.S. over-the-counter pharmaceuticals market, even though it included few major brand-name products..
He noted that the over-the-counter pharmaceuticals market was growing at a faster rate than the prescription drug market.
